config.title: 4 Days in Berlin - FAQ
config.subtitle: How to use the fourth day, what each option really costs in hours, and the closures that catch people out.

items.a: **Yes, and it is the first trip length that gives you a choice.** Three days cover the historic centre, the divided city and one museum plus one neighbourhood. The fourth day is free, which is why it is worth planning rather than improvising: it is the day you can leave the city, go deep into one district, or slow down and do one thing properly.

items.q: What should I do on my fourth day in Berlin?
items.a: **Pick the shape before the place.** Go far (Potsdam, Sachsenhausen, the Spreewald), go deep (Köpenick, Charlottenburg, the Wannsee) or go slow (one Museum Island collection). Guests who pick the place first usually pick the furthest one and then spend the day on trains.

items.q: How long does a day trip to Potsdam from Berlin take?
items.a: **About seven hours all in.** The S7 reaches Potsdam Hauptbahnhof in 42 minutes from Alexanderplatz and a bus adds about 16 more to Schloss Sanssouci, so roughly two hours of travel plus a sensible five hours on the ground. Below six hours it stops being worth it. Potsdam is in zone C, so you need an ABC ticket.

items.q: Is Sachsenhausen a full day from Berlin?
items.a: **No, three hours on site is a complete visit**, so with about 52 minutes each way it fits into a shorter day than most people expect. Entry is free, the grounds and exhibitions open 08:30 to 18:00 until 26 October and 08:30 to 16:30 after that, and an audio guide costs 3.50 euros. I would keep the evening free afterwards.

items.q: What can I do in Berlin if I only have four or five free hours?
items.a: **Stay inside the city.** Tempelhofer Feld is 19 minutes away on the U5 and U6 and free to enter, Charlottenburg Palace is 24 minutes, and Museumsinsel is three minutes on the U5. A short day out of town is worse than a long day in town.

items.q: Which Berlin day trips close on Mondays?
items.a: **Sanssouci Palace, Charlottenburg Palace and most of the Museum Island houses are closed on Mondays.** That removes three of the eight fourth-day options at once. Tempelhofer Feld, the Sachsenhausen Memorial, Köpenick, the Wannsee ferry and the Spreewald boats all still run.

items.q: Do I need a different transport ticket for a day trip from Berlin?
items.a: **For Potsdam and Oranienburg, yes: both are in zone C, so an AB ticket does not reach them.** Buy ABC. The Deutschlandticket covers all of it including the regional trains to the Spreewald. Trips inside Berlin, like Köpenick, Wannsee, Charlottenburg and Tempelhofer Feld, stay within zones AB.
